note: Each seed = independent BB84 decoy-state dataset generation + full LSTM/RF/static-baseline training+eval pipeline (section 16 of the notebook). Reported as mean +/- std per method/split, per the notebook's own reporting guidance (cell 48).
headline_finding: On PNS_only (the QBER-silent attack), the naive QBER-only static threshold nearly collapses (PR-AUC 0.1543 +/- 0.0355, barely above a random detector) -- this part of the motivation is fully confirmed. However, this table's 'Static QBER+throughput (per-link)' row is a stronger, still-zero-ML baseline (a plain rule combining QBER with sifted-key throughput drop) that already recovers most of the performance (PR-AUC 0.7803 +/- 0.0300). Random Forest (0.8005 +/- 0.0294) and the LSTM (0.8527 +/- 0.0234) both improve further on top of that, with the LSTM ahead by a real but modest ~5-7 points of PR-AUC over the combined rule/RF -- not a dramatic rescue. The correct headline is: QBER alone is genuinely broken on PNS, feature engineering (informed by decoy-state theory) closes most of that gap even without ML, and sequence modeling adds a smaller, consistent improvement on top while giving a single unified detector for both attack types. On IR_only (the loud attack), the static threshold performs comparably to the LSTM, as expected since that is the case it was originally designed to catch. Low std across all 7 independently-generated seeds indicates all of the above is not a single-seed artifact. See qkd/single_seed_results.json for the underlying per-feature analysis (feature importances, standalone per-feature AUCs, and a no-leakage sanity check) that this finding is based on.
caveats: Multi-seed loop reruns LSTM, Random Forest, and both static baselines per seed; it does NOT rerun the Logistic Regression baseline from the single-seed run (noted as a known gap in the notebook itself, cell 48).

Per-seed raw rows (multiseed_results_raw.csv) live only on the team's Google Drive (Colab session), not in this repo -- only the aggregated mean/std/count summary was recoverable from the notebook's saved output cells.
